# Functional Narrative: Mixing Tank Module (Upgrade FDS Draft)

**Basis:** The technician's SLC-500 logic export (R0–R6) and their notes. Nothing here has been field-verified. All tags are **provisional** (see OI-01). The as-found PLC addresses are shown for traceability only.

**Provisional tag map**

| Provisional tag | As-found address | Description | As-found polarity |
|---|---|---|---|
| TK-100 | — | Mixing tank | — |
| HS-100 | I:1/2 ESTOP_OK | E-stop healthy | ON = healthy |
| HS-101 | I:1/0 START_PB | Start pushbutton | ON = pressed |
| HS-102 | I:1/1 STOP_PB | Stop pushbutton (NC) | ON = healthy |
| HS-103 | I:1/5 AGIT_HAND | Agitator selector, panel door | ON = HAND |
| LSL-102 | I:1/3 LSL_TANK | Tank low level switch | ON = level above low point (per tech) |
| LSH-101 | I:1/4 LSH_TANK | Tank high level switch | ON = high (inferred from logic, **unverified**) |
| TSL-103 | I:1/6 TEMP_LOW | Tank low temperature switch | ON = below switch point (inferred) |
| XV-101 | O:2/0 FILL_VLV | Fill valve | ON = open |
| M-101 | O:2/1 AGITATOR | Agitator motor | ON = run |
| XV-102 | O:2/2 STEAM_VLV | Steam valve | ON = open |
| XA-104 | O:2/3 ALARM_HORN | Alarm horn | ON = sound |

---

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

TK-100 holds, mixes, and heats product. XV-101 keeps the level at LSH-101, and XV-102 holds the temperature at TSL-103. M-101 mixes when the level is above LSL-102.

- **Upstream:** Fill supply through XV-101. Steam supply through XV-102.
- **Downstream:** Not controlled by this logic. The discharge path is unknown (OI-03).
- **Model:** The as-found logic is continuous (hold level and temperature). This narrative uses ISA-106. If the process is really a batch (fill, mix, heat, discharge), move it to ISA-88 (OI-02).

## 2. Equipment and tags

Refer to the instrument index (OI-01). Until it is issued, use the provisional tag map above.

## 3. States and transitions

| State | Description | Entry permissives | Initiator | Allowed exits | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| STOPPED | XV-101 and XV-102 closed. M-101 stopped. | None | Operator STOP complete, power restore, E-stop reset | STARTING | Operator-prompted |
| STARTING | Start permissives checked | HS-100 healthy, HS-102 healthy, no fill fault, HS-101 not held, power-restore message acknowledged | Operator START (rising edge) | RUNNING, STOPPED, ESTOPPED | Automatic |
| RUNNING | Level, agitator, and heating control active | From STARTING only | Automatic | FILL FAULT, STOPPING, ESTOPPED | Automatic |
| FILL FAULT | XV-101 closed. M-101 and XV-102 per OI-04. | Fill timeout | Automatic | RUNNING (operator RESET), STOPPING, ESTOPPED | Operator-prompted |
| STOPPING | Stop sequence (SEQ-2) | Any of RUNNING, FILL FAULT | Operator STOP, or HS-102 open | STOPPED, ESTOPPED | Automatic |
| ESTOPPED | Outputs de-energized by hardwired circuit | HS-100 not healthy | Automatic | STOPPED only (E-stop reset + operator RESET) | Operator-prompted |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-MIX100-001 | The module must have only the states in the state table. | Inspection + test each transition |
| FR-MIX100-002 | After power restore, the module must go to STOPPED, whatever the state was before the power loss. | Test: cycle power in RUNNING |
| FR-MIX100-003 | START must act on the rising edge of HS-101 only. | Test: hold HS-101, operate STOP, release STOP |
| FR-MIX100-004 | If HS-101 stays on for longer than the start-held time, the module must reject START and raise an alarm. | Test: force HS-101 on |
| FR-MIX100-005 | START must not reset the fill timer or a fill fault. | Test: press START in FILL FAULT |
| FR-MIX100-006 | In STARTING, if a permissive is not met, the module must go to STOPPED and show the missing permissive. | Test each permissive |
| FR-MIX100-007 | Operations must sign off the state table and all prompts. | Inspection: signed record |

## 4. Regulatory control

No tuning values are needed. All loops are on/off.

**Level, XV-101 (PV: LSH-101)**
- Active in RUNNING only. XV-101 is closed in all other states.
- Open XV-101 when LSH-101 is clear for longer than the fill-restart delay.
- Close XV-101 when LSH-101 is active for longer than the switch debounce time.

**Agitator, M-101 (permissive: LSL-102)**
- Active in RUNNING and FILL FAULT (OI-04).
- Run M-101 when LSL-102 is active for longer than the switch debounce time.
- Stop M-101 when LSL-102 is clear for longer than the switch debounce time.
- HS-103 must not bypass LSL-102 (see DNC-07, OI-05).

**Temperature, XV-102 (PV: TSL-103)**
- Open XV-102 only when all three are true: TSL-103 active, M-101 run feedback active, and LSL-102 active.
- Close XV-102 when any of the three is false.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-MIX100-010 | XV-101 must open only in RUNNING with LSH-101 clear for the fill-restart delay. | Test: simulate LSH-101 |
| FR-MIX100-011 | XV-101 must close when LSH-101 is active for the debounce time. | Test |
| FR-MIX100-012 | The fill timer must measure each fill cycle separately and reset when XV-101 closes on LSH-101. | Test: several short fills that together exceed the fill timeout must not trip |
| FR-MIX100-013 | If one fill cycle exceeds the fill timeout, the module must go to FILL FAULT. | Test |
| FR-MIX100-014 | M-101 must not run when LSL-102 is clear, in any mode. | Test: HS-103 in each position, LSL-102 clear |
| FR-MIX100-015 | If M-101 run feedback is not active within the agitator start time, the module must remove the M-101 command and alarm. | Test: hold feedback off |
| FR-MIX100-016 | XV-102 must open only when TSL-103, M-101 run feedback, and LSL-102 are all active. | Test each condition false |
| FR-MIX100-017 | If LSH-101 is active and LSL-102 is clear, the module must alarm a level switch disagreement and close XV-101. | Test |

## 5. Sequences

**SEQ-1 Start** (from STARTING)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | Check all start permissives. | All permissives true | Immediate check, no wait | Go to STOPPED. Show the missing permissive. |
| 20 | Reset the fill timer. Enable level, agitator, and temperature control. | Control enabled | Immediate, no wait | Not applicable |
| 30 | Go to RUNNING. | — | — | — |

**SEQ-2 Stop** (from STOPPING)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | Close XV-102. Close XV-101. | Commands off (and closed limits, if added under OI-06) | Valve travel time | Alarm "valve fail to close". Continue to step 20. |
| 20 | Keep M-101 on for the agitator run-on time. | Run-on time complete | Agitator run-on time | Not applicable |
| 30 | Stop M-101. | M-101 run feedback off | Agitator stop time | Alarm "M-101 fail to stop". Go to STOPPED with alarm active. |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-MIX100-020 | SEQ-1 and SEQ-2 must operate as the step tables show, including each failure response. | Test each step and each failure |

## 6. Interlocks and permissives

Refer to the cause-and-effect chart CE-MIX100 (OI-07). Draft rows for that chart:

| Cause | XV-101 | M-101 | XV-102 |
|---|---|---|---|
| HS-100 not healthy (hardwired) | Close | Stop | Close |
| LSH-101 active | Close | — | — |
| LSL-102 clear | — | Stop | Close |
| M-101 run feedback off | — | — | Close |
| Fill timeout | Close | Per OI-04 | Per OI-04 |
| Level switch disagreement | Close | — | — |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-MIX100-030 | The E-stop must remove power from XV-101, M-101, and XV-102 through a hardwired safety circuit, independent of the PLC. | Test: E-stop with PLC in program mode |
| FR-MIX100-031 | Any high-level or high-temperature safety function found by the hazard review must go in the SRS, not in this document. | Inspection |

## 7. Alarms

Refer to the rationalized alarm database. Candidates to submit for rationalization: fill timeout, M-101 fail to start, M-101 fail to stop, valve fail to close, START held, level switch disagreement, E-stop active, power restored.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-MIX100-040 | Silence, acknowledge, and fault reset must be separate operator actions. | Test |
| FR-MIX100-041 | Silencing XA-104 must not change any valve or motor command. | Test: silence in FILL FAULT |

## 8. Abnormal handling

| Condition | Response | ID / Test |
|---|---|---|
| Power loss | Field devices go to fail position (below). | FR-MIX100-050, test |
| Power restore | Go to STOPPED. Clear the run state and fill timer. Show "power restored" prompt. Wait for operator START. | FR-MIX100-051, test |
| PLC fault or I/O comms loss | I/O modules de-energize all outputs. | FR-MIX100-052, test: pull I/O comms |
| HMI comms loss | Hold the current state. HS-102 and HS-100 stay functional. | FR-MIX100-053, test |
| Bad PV (open wire), LSL-102 | Reads clear: M-101 stops, XV-102 closes. This is safe. | FR-MIX100-054, test |
| Bad PV (open wire), LSH-101 | As-found reads "not high", so filling continues. This is **not** safe. Wire so an open circuit reads "high" (DNC-05). | FR-MIX100-055, test: lift wire |
| Bad PV (open wire), TSL-103 | Reads "not low": XV-102 closes. This is safe. A switch stuck active is not detected (DNC-10). | FR-MIX100-056, test |
| Fail positions | XV-101 fail closed. XV-102 fail closed. M-101 stops. Confirm in field (OI-06). | FR-MIX100-057, inspection + test |

## 9. Operator interface

- **Shows:** Module state, missing permissives, XV-101, M-101, and XV-102 command and feedback, switch states, fill time remaining, and active alarms.
- **Operator can:** START, STOP, SILENCE, ACKNOWLEDGE, and RESET (fill fault, E-stop, power restore).
- **Prompts:** "Power restored. Push START to run." / "Fill fault. Find the cause. Push RESET." / "E-stop reset. Push RESET."
- **Requirement:** FR-MIX100-060: Operations must sign off all prompt text (inspection).

## 10. Open items

Dates are placeholders. Set them at FDS kickoff.

| OI-03 | Define the discharge path and any discharge control. | Process engineer | [date] |
| OI-04 | In FILL FAULT, decide if M-101 and XV-102 continue or stop. | Process + Operations | [date] |
| OI-05 | Decide what HS-103 is for. Remove it, or replace it with a maintenance mode that keeps LSL-102 active. | Operations | [date] |
| OI-06 | Field-verify switch polarity, valve fail positions, and M-101 run feedback. Add limit switches if needed. | I&E technician | [date] |
| OI-07 | Issue CE-MIX100. | Controls lead | [date] |
| OI-08 | Run a hazard review for overfill and overtemperature. Issue SRS items if needed. | Process safety | [date] |
| OI-09 | Verify if HS-100 is hardwired or PLC-only. | I&E technician | [date] |
| OI-10 | Consider an LT and TT to replace the switches for control. Keep switches as independent protection. | Process + Controls | [date] |

| Item | As-found | Proposed |

| Fill timeout | 600 s, cumulative (RTO) | Per fill cycle, value TBD (Process) |
| Fill-restart delay | None | TBD |

## Do not carry forward

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| DNC-01 | R0 | **Auto-restart on power return.** The seal-in bit B3:0/0 keeps its value through a power cycle. The rung re-seals on the first scan, so the tank refills with nobody present. The technician saw this happen. | Make the run state non-retentive. Reset it on the first scan. Require START (FR-002). |
| DNC-02 | R0 | START is level-sensitive. If START is held or stuck, the unit restarts as soon as STOP is released. | Use rising-edge START with a start-held alarm (FR-003, FR-004). |
| DNC-03 | R6 | START resets the fill timer. That silences the horn and reopens XV-101 with no check of the cause. Pressing START repeatedly defeats the fill timeout. | Use a separate RESET. Keep silence separate (FR-005, FR-040, FR-041). |
| DNC-04 | R2 | The RTO adds up fill time across all top-ups and across power cycles. It resets only on START, not on STOP. Long runs will nuisance-trip. | Use a per-fill timer that resets when each fill completes (FR-012). |
| DNC-05 | R1 | LSH-101 appears to be energize-on-high. A broken wire reads "not high" and the tank overfills. One switch does both control and protection. | Wire it to fail to "high". Add independent high-high protection if the hazard review requires it (OI-08). |
| DNC-06 | R1 | There is no debounce or deadband on LSH-101. XV-101 will chatter at the switch point. | Add debounce and restart delay (FR-010, FR-011). |
| DNC-07 | R3 | HS-103 (HAND) bypasses the low-level permissive. M-101 can run dry or with the impeller uncovered. HAND is also not a true hand mode, because it still needs the run latch. | Remove the bypass (FR-014, OI-05). |
| DNC-08 | R4 | Steam is permitted by the M-101 *command*, not by proof of running. If M-101 trips on overload, steam stays on with no mixing. | Interlock to run feedback (FR-016). |
| DNC-09 | R3→R4 | Through DNC-07, steam can open with the level below LSL-102. That heats with the coil or jacket uncovered. | Add LSL-102 to the steam permissive (FR-016). |
| DNC-10 | R4 | There is no high-temperature protection. If TSL-103 sticks active, steam runs without limit. | Hazard review. Add a TSH or TT. SIS goes to the SRS if required (OI-08, OI-10). |
| DNC-11 | R5 | The horn is the only alarm. It covers fill timeout only. It cannot be silenced without pressing START. | Use the rationalized alarm list with silence and acknowledge (Section 7). |
| DNC-12 | R0 | The E-stop may be a PLC input only. If it is, it does not meet hardwired E-stop practice (NFPA 79 / IEC 60204-1). | Verify (OI-09). Use a hardwired safety relay (FR-030). |
| DNC-13 | All | No tag numbers or documentation, and polarity is known only from technician notes. | Field-verify before FAT (OI-01, OI-06). |

**Highest priority:** DNC-01, DNC-05, DNC-07/09, and DNC-12. These four can cause unattended filling, overfill, or dry-running and heating. Verify them in the field on the existing system now, not only in the upgrade. DNC-01 has already occurred.

## Checks

- SSoT: done. All values are in SP-MIX100, and the as-found 600 s appears only there.
- IDs and tests: done.
- States: each state has entry permissives and exits.
- Sequence timeouts: done. Logic-only steps are marked as immediate.
- Abnormal handling: done.
- Interlocks and alarms: referenced.
- SIS: deferred to the SRS.
- STE pass: applied to the narrative text.
- Open items: owners assigned. **Dates are still blank.**
